title: Sorting and Filtering Data in SQLite
description: A short, hands-on course teaching beginner data analysts how to browse, sort, and filter e-commerce order data directly in the DB Browser for SQLite UI before writing any SQL.

videos.title: Browse the Orders Table
videos.learning_objective: Recognize the structure of a raw data table before manipulating it with sorting or filtering.
videos.discovery_objective: Open the Orders table in the Browse Data tab, identify the 5 columns (order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status) by name, scroll through the first page of rows, and note that some status cells appear blank.

exercise_artifact.description: A two-table dataset of customers and their orders used to demonstrate sorting and filtering in DB Browser for SQLite.

videos.new_capability: Open a table in the Browse Data tab
videos.running_example_usage: Learner opens the Orders table for the e-commerce dataset and inspects its columns and rows.
videos.proof_numbers: The Orders table contains 500 rows and 5 columns, with 42 rows showing a blank status value.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll sort the amount column in the Browse Data tab by clicking its column header.

videos.title: Sort Orders by Amount
videos.learning_objective: Use column sorting to quickly identify extreme values in a dataset.
videos.discovery_objective: Click the amount column header in the Orders table's Browse Data tab to sort rows in ascending order, then click again to sort descending.

exercise_artifact.description: A two-table dataset of customers and their orders used to demonstrate sorting and filtering in DB Browser for SQLite.

videos.new_capability: Sort a column by clicking its header
videos.running_example_usage: Learner sorts the 500 Orders rows by the amount column to find the smallest and largest orders.
videos.proof_numbers: Ascending sort places a $12.50 order at the top; descending sort places a $998.75 order at the top.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we opened the Orders table and saw 500 rows across 5 columns, including 42 blank status cells.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter Orders by an exact status match using the column filter box.

videos.title: Filter Orders by Exact Status
videos.learning_objective: Isolate rows matching a specific category value using UI filtering.
videos.discovery_objective: Type 'Shipped' into the status column's filter box in the Orders table's Browse Data tab to display only matching rows.

exercise_artifact.description: A two-table dataset of customers and their orders used to demonstrate sorting and filtering in DB Browser for SQLite.

videos.new_capability: Filter rows by exact text match
videos.running_example_usage: Learner filters the Orders table to show only rows where status equals 'Shipped'.
videos.proof_numbers: The filter reduces 500 total rows to 210 rows where status equals 'Shipped'.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we sorted 500 orders by amount, finding a $12.50 order at the low end and a $998.75 order at the high end.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter Orders by a numeric comparison on the amount column using the filter box.

videos.title: Filter Orders by Amount Threshold
videos.learning_objective: Narrow a dataset to rows exceeding a numeric threshold using UI filtering.
videos.discovery_objective: Type '>500' into the amount column's filter box in the Orders table's Browse Data tab to display only rows above that value.

exercise_artifact.description: A two-table dataset of customers and their orders used to demonstrate sorting and filtering in DB Browser for SQLite.

videos.running_example_usage: Learner filters the Orders table to show only orders with an amount greater than 500.
videos.proof_numbers: The filter reduces 500 total rows to 76 rows where amount is greater than 500.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we filtered 500 orders down to 210 rows with status equal to 'Shipped'.
